claims.text: A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ in the Pulumi docs (the target of the 'Provider support policy' card on the support index page).
The Pulumi provider support policy page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
The Pulumi provider support policy page describes which providers get long-term security updates (implying some Pulumi providers receive long-term security updates).
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The Pulumi provider support policy page (/docs/support/provider-support-policy/) lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi-maintained providers receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry (/registry/) shows the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
The page /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (Provider support policy) exists as a link target.
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes during an update if an error or failure occurs; it completes pending in-progress operations, then exits and reports the error.
Pulumi does not automatically query the cloud provider's live state before running `pulumi up` or `pulumi preview`.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes state and applies the desired state in a single step.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection for automated drift detection and remediation on a schedule.
Pulumi auto-naming appends a random suffix to the logical name, and this lets Pulumi replace resources with less downtime by creating the replacement before deleting the old one.
For every stack, Pulumi Cloud manages a unique encryption key used to encrypt secrets for that stack, and this is configurable to use a custom secrets provider.
`pulumi config set --secret` encrypts the value so it can be persisted in `Pulumi.<stack-name>.yaml`.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine in any way, but some Pulumi providers use the open-source Terraform schemas.
Pulumi native providers are mapped directly to cloud provider APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.
Experimental Pulumi features are always opt-in, enabled with a flag, command, or environment variable such as `PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true`, and can change or be removed without a deprecation cycle.
In npm, the tilde operator (~1.2.3) allows patch updates on the current minor version.

Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic to smooth the upgrade from the immediately previous major version, but these migrations do not always work across multiple major versions.
Minor provider versions typically include new resources and features, performance improvements, and bug fixes without breaking changes.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version (N-1) for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers receiving long-term support updates on eligible older versions are AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
The provider list links to Registry package pages at /registry/packages/aws/, azure/, azure-native/, azuread/, command/, docker-build/, gcp/, kubernetes/, tls/, and vault/, which must exist.

A Pulumi provider LTS release contains High/Critical CVE security patches: fixes for CVEs affecting the provider's code or direct dependencies, and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship them.

A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
LTS providers remain compatible with the version of Pulumi they were frozen at unless security fixes require otherwise.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.
When major N+1 ships, it becomes the new N, the old N becomes the new LTS major, and the previous LTS major reaches end of life the same day regardless of remaining 12-month window.
Within the LTS major, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
LTS provider releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version automatically receive patch releases as they ship, and pinning to a major version is recommended.
Older majors (N-2 and earlier) of a covered provider receive no patches; if v3 is newest, v2 is N-1 and v1 and earlier are end of life.
The current major (N) receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
End-of-life versions (N-2 and older) are not supported and receive no updates.
The FAQ page /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/ has an anchor 'what-are-the-best-practices-for-maintaining-provider-versions'.
Pages /registry/ and /docs/support/getting-support/ exist.
